messages.author: 9d7d423218727f97
messages.subject: Figure labels: numbering and identifying
parts:
I have two questions, which I suspect are related.
1. Why are both figures numbered as figure 1?
2. Is there a way to label figures that can be reference in the text without directly using the LateX label syntax. In my example below, I tried three different labels within the chunk header without success with the first plot  while the standard LateX syntax worked fine for the second figure except that it is also numbered as figure 1.

\documentclass{article}
\usepackage{float}
\begin{document}
\section{Intro}
<<load_data, echo = TRUE, include = TRUE>>=
test <- rnorm(100, 0, 1)
@
<<hist, echo = TRUE, include = TRUE, fig.cap = "A histogram", fig.show = 'asis', fig.ref = 'hist1', fig.label = 'hist2'>>=
hist(test)
@
The histogram is Figure \ref{hist}, \ref{hist1}, or \ref{hist2}
\begin{figure}[H]
<<boxplot, echo = TRUE, include = TRUE, fig.show = 'asis'>>=
boxplot(test)
@
\label{boxplot}
\end{figure}
The boxplot is Figure \ref{boxplot}.
\end{document}

messages.author: cc1ef8c8158d6b73
messages.subject: Re: [knitr] Figure labels: numbering and identifying
parts:
1. Again, this is a LaTeX problem; if your figure does not have a
\caption{}, it will not be numbered in the figure sequence.

2. Read the documentation of fig.lp in
http://yihui.name/knitr/options; the real label for the figure is not
the chunk label by default, so \ref{hist} will not work (as you can
see the question marks in PDF).

Regards,
Yihui
